mission: Ridgeline above the new seal's hum. Torin on the edge, posture unchanged, presence diminished — warmth muted, humor gone quiet, Force-presence lighter in a way that should feel freeing and is devastating. Sera has chosen to remain temporarily at the Veranthos recovery and debriefing site with him, not as a Jedi asset but as a displaced survivor with agency. She walks up and sits beside him without speaking. After a long time, his hand finds hers. Lighter grip than before. It is there.
why_now: The Sera/Torin arc has to land in an image, not a speech. The hand on a hand on a ridgeline is the final word on love without control.
conflict: There is nothing to fix. Torin is partly present and partly not. Sera does not try to fix him. The scene's argument is that presence is the thing, and presence does not require the person to be whole.
turning_point: Torin's hand finds Sera's. The grip is lighter than before. It is there.
opening_hook: Torin sits on the ridgeline with his hands resting on his knees, facing the valley where the new seal hums. His posture is the same as before. Everything else is different.
closing_hook: Sera sits beside Torin. She doesn't speak. He doesn't either. After a long time, his hand finds hers. The grip is lighter than it was. But it's there.
emotional_trajectory: Quiet grief -> the devastation of partial success -> the grace of staying

setting: Veranthos — ridgeline, overlooking the valley where the new seal hums
sensory_details: Torin's diminished presence — lighter, quieter, the heavy warmth gone; the recovery shelter lights below the ridge, not a Temple intake line or recruitment station; Sera's field kit and debrief slate set aside by her own hand; Sera's face holding grief and peace without choosing between them; their hands touching in a grip lighter than before; the new seal humming in the valley below, three-part harmony audible in the Force

notes: Sera's arc resolves in chosen presence; Torin's arc resolves tragic in diminished survival. key_beats.beat_description: Torin sits on the ridgeline with his hands resting on his knees, facing the valley where the new seal hums. His posture is unchanged from before. Everything else is different — his presence lighter, the heavy warmth gone quiet, his Force-signature diminished in a way that should feel freeing and is devastating.
key_beats.state_change: The abstract pressure of Torin's sacrifice becomes concrete and visible. Ben can see what the sealing cost him.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's instinct pushes toward action — the impulse to do something, to fix, to restore — but there is nothing to fix. The grief is quiet because the work is done. His attention tightens on the small details: the angle of Torin's shoulders, the way his hands rest, the absence of the warmth that used to radiate from him.

key_beats.beat_description: Sera walks up the ridgeline and sits beside Torin without speaking. She does not try to fill the silence. She does not offer comfort as a solution. She simply sits.
key_beats.state_change: The scene pivots from Ben's observation of loss to the arrival of presence. Sera's choice to sit without speaking becomes the argument itself.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben feels the shift in the air between them — not a lightening, but a settling. The pressure does not ease; it transforms. He recognizes in Sera's face the same grief and peace holding together without choosing between them. This is what staying looks like.

key_beats.beat_description: After a long time — long enough that the new seal's three-part harmonic hum becomes the only sound — Torin's hand finds Sera's. The grip is lighter than it was before. But it is there.
key_beats.state_change: The hand-grip becomes the final word on the Sera/Torin relationship: love as presence, not as fixing. Torin's diminished survival is accepted. Sera's choice to stay is complete.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben registers this as the grace of staying — the recognition that presence without wholeness is the only victory available, and it is enough. The cost lands on him as witness: he cannot restore what was lost, and the people he cares for have accepted a future smaller than before. This is not failure. This is what survival looks like when the alternative is dissolution.

anti_patterns: Sera and Torin do not speak in this scene; the hand is the sentence
Ben observes from a distance; interiority minimal — a single line of observation, maybe, and the rest is the wind and the ridgeline and the hum below
Do not arrive at clinical articulation of what the hand-grip means — let the image carry the meaning
